identity.name: XDM Container Telemetry Normalization — Modeling-Rule Substrate Proof (T1610 / T1613)
identity.summary: Prove the full raw-source to detection chain for container telemetry: an XDM modeling rule maps the raw actor_container_info JSON blob into addressable XDM fields (pod_namespace, image_name, privileged), and a BIOC then fires on the normalized privileged field. The modeling rule is the normalization substrate beneath the detection — it enables firing, it does not itself fire.
identity.description: Cortex detections assume data is already normalized into the Cortex Data Model (XDM), but a real DC onboarding a customer log source must first author the parsing/modeling rules that map raw event JSON into addressable XDM fields. Modeling rules are XQL written under a [MODEL: dataset=...] declaration; normalization is opt-in per source (schema-on-read), so an un-modeled log stays searchable but is NOT analytics-grade — modeling rules are therefore the gating substrate for analytics-grade detection. This entry brings that substrate into the corpus as a first-class, paste-able card kind (detections.modeling_rules[]) and proves the chain end-to-end against container telemetry. The modeling rule is derived from the real xsiam-prisma-cdr-lab container_info.sql: it reads the raw actor_container_info JSON the Linux agent daemonset emits and json_extract_scalar's it into normalized fields — pod_namespace, pod_name, image_name, image_id, container_id, and the security-relevant privileged flag. With those fields modeled, a BIOC fires on privileged container starts (the normalized privileged = true field), and a validation XQL confirms the modeled fields are populated. The card deliberately does NOT add a sixth detection_type: a modeling rule does not fire, it enables firing, so the coverage rollup counts it informationally only. The point of the scenario is to let a DC show the moment a raw, un-analytics-grade log source becomes analytics-grade — the raw blob, the [MODEL: ...] rule, the now-addressable privileged field, and the BIOC that fires on it.

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-CDR-015 — raw container telemetry to XDM-normalized field to BIOC chain proof

prerequisites.description: Cortex XSIAM with the Linux agent daemonset deployed so raw actor_container_info telemetry reaches the tenant.
prerequisites.check_command: kubectl -n kube-system get daemonset | grep -i cortex

prerequisites.description: cdr IaC module applied so the EKS cluster with worker nodes exists and is reachable via kubeconfig.

payload.code:
# No detonation. Start a privileged container so the agent emits raw
# actor_container_info telemetry the modeling rule normalizes into XDM fields.
set -euo pipefail
kubectl run cortexsim-priv-probe --image=public.ecr.aws/docker/library/busybox:1.36 --restart=Never --overrides='{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"p","image":"public.ecr.aws/docker/library/busybox:1.36","command":["sh","-c","id; sleep 60"],"securityContext":{"privileged":true}}]}}' || true
kubectl wait --for=condition=Ready pod/cortexsim-priv-probe --timeout=120s || true

input_variables.name: TARGET_NS
input_variables.description: Namespace the privileged probe pod is started in.

expected_artifacts.description: A privileged container start whose raw actor_container_info JSON carries privileged=true, normalized by the modeling rule into the XDM privileged field.

cleanup.code: kubectl delete pod cortexsim-priv-probe --ignore-not-found; echo '[CortexSim] SIM-CDR-015 cleanup complete.'

modeling_rules.name: Container Telemetry XDM Normalization
modeling_rules.description: Maps the raw actor_container_info JSON blob the Linux agent emits into addressable XDM container fields. Derived from the xsiam-prisma-cdr-lab container_info.sql. This is the normalization substrate beneath the privileged-container BIOC — it enables firing, it does not itself fire.
modeling_rules.logic:
[MODEL: dataset = cortexsim_container_raw]
| fields actor_container_info as container_info
| filter container_info != null
| alter pod_namespace = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.pod_namespace")
| alter pod_name = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.pod_name")
| alter image_name = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.image_name")
| alter image_id = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.image_id")
| alter container_id = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.id")
| alter privileged = json_extract_scalar(container_info, "$.privileged")

biocs.name: CDR-XDM Privileged Container Start on Modeled Field
biocs.description: Fires on a container start where the modeled privileged field (normalized from the raw actor_container_info blob by the modeling rule) is true. This BIOC only works BECAUSE the modeling rule made privileged addressable — proving the raw-source to modeled-field to detection chain.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter actor_container_info != null
| alter privileged = json_extract_scalar(actor_container_info, "$.privileged")
| filter privileged = "true"
| fields agent_hostname, actor_process_image_name, privileged
| comp count() as privileged_starts by agent_hostname
| filter privileged_starts >= 1

xql_queries.name: CDR-XDM Modeled Container Fields Populated
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 600)
| filter actor_container_info != null
| alter pod_namespace = json_extract_scalar(actor_container_info, "$.pod_namespace")
| alter privileged = json_extract_scalar(actor_container_info, "$.privileged")
| filter pod_namespace != null
| comp count() as modeled_events by pod_namespace, privileged
| filter modeled_events >= 1
| fields pod_namespace, privileged, modeled_events

products.evidence_query: The modeling rule normalizes raw actor_container_info into XDM fields; the BIOC fires on the modeled privileged field, proving the raw-source to detection chain.

threat_scenarios.name: XDM Normalization Substrate Proof for Container Telemetry
threat_scenarios.description: A DC proves the full raw-source to detection chain: an XDM modeling rule maps raw container JSON into addressable fields, and a BIOC fires on the normalized privileged field.

threat_steps.objective: The modeling rule normalizes raw container telemetry and the privileged-container BIOC fires on the modeled field.
preconditions: cdr EKS fixture applied with the Cortex Linux agent daemonset deployed.
A privileged container started so raw actor_container_info telemetry is emitted.
steps: Apply the modeling rule that normalizes actor_container_info into XDM fields.
Observe the modeled fields populate and the privileged-container BIOC fire.
success_criteria: Validation XQL `CDR-XDM Modeled Container Fields Populated` returns >= 1 event with privileged populated.
BIOC `CDR-XDM Privileged Container Start on Modeled Field` fires on the modeled privileged field.

preventive_controls: Forbid privileged containers via admission control (OPA/Gatekeeper or Kyverno) and Pod Security Standards.
Author and maintain XDM modeling rules for every onboarded container log source so all container telemetry is analytics-grade.
Run service workloads as non-root with no privilege escalation.
detection_engineering: Model raw container telemetry into XDM fields before authoring container detections — un-modeled logs are searchable but not analytics-grade.
Alert on container starts whose modeled privileged field is true outside an approved exception list.
Validate that newly onboarded log sources populate their expected XDM fields before relying on downstream detections.

references.title: Cortex XSIAM — XDM data modeling rules (parsing and modeling)
